# Prism roof transport: exact original-volume lift and its height defect

This note specializes the archived boundary martingale and Gauss–Green
identities to actual prisms. The new point is the exact change of law
needed to turn a roof transport into an original-volume transport. It
identifies a necessary and sufficient equality condition for that lift
to remain a physical martingale. The condition is not implied by the
normal-convex stress inequality. No OC or joint-minimum classification
is claimed.

Dependencies already proved in this workspace:

* `candidate 22fb802a1dc82eb3` and
  `candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb`
  prove general boundary variance and polynomial Gauss–Green identities;
* `candidate 7234d49b6c886f4b`, §§7–8,
  supplies separate upper/lower same-normal convex order under one
  common normal-dependent stress;
* `candidate 9158d8d941246660`
  and its independent audits establish that cone at the selected
  positive-buffer minima. Passing to an ordinary stress still requires
  the separately proved normal-recorded limit and vanishing correction.

## 1. Actual geometry and one roof law

Let (P\subset\mathbb Z^n) be finite and complete in its convex hull.
Write the continuous coordinates as ((X,y)\in\mathbb R^{d-1}\times\mathbb R),
where (d\ge1). Let

\[
 K_z=B_z\times[-H_z,H_z],\qquad H_z>0,
 \quad \mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes1_{K_z}\,dX\,dy,
 \quad M=\mu(S).
\]

The (B_z) are positive-volume convex bodies and are compatible under
all anchored barycentric relations; (H_z) is sampled concave. These
conditions ensure that the canonical hull has exactly the stated
integer fibers. For (d=1), use the singleton (B_z\subset\mathbb R^0)
with its zero-dimensional mass one.

The upper-roof measure is

\[
 \eta=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes1_{B_z}\,dX\otimes\delta_{H_z}.
\]

A roof point is (s=(\xi,H)=(z,X,H_z)). Suppose a finite measure
\(\nu\) on this same roof has a martingale coupling \(\Pi\) to
\(\eta\). Disintegrate

\[
 \Pi(ds,ds')=\nu(ds)P_s(ds'),\qquad
 \int(\xi',H')P_s(ds')=(\xi,H).                  \tag{1}
\]

In the stress application, \(d\nu=(W^+/\beta)d\eta\), where (W^+)
is the actual allocated upper-roof captured fraction. Only this
martingale hypothesis is used below. In particular,

\[
 \int2H\,d\nu=\int2H\,d\eta=M.                \tag{2}
\]

## 2. The original-volume lift

Let (t\) be uniform on ([-1,1]), with probability law (dt/2).
Weight the joint roof law by **target height** and set

\[
 d\Omega=2H'\,d\Pi\,\frac{dt}{2},\qquad
 w=(\xi,tH),\quad w'=(\xi',tH').               \tag{3}
\]

The second marginal of this measure is exactly \(\mu\): conditional
on a target roof point, (2H'\,dt/2\) is Lebesgue measure on its actual
vertical column. By (1), the first marginal is the vertical-column
lift of (2H\nu\). In the stress application it is

\[
 d\mu_W(w)=\frac{W^+(z,X)}{\beta}\,d\mu(w).     \tag{4}
\]

Both marginals therefore have the original mass (M). This is one
common coupling, not separate capwise couplings.

The conditional target law given (w=(\xi,tH)) is the height-biased
row

\[
 P_s^H(ds')=\frac{H'}H P_s(ds').                \tag{5}
\]

Consequently its **physical** barycenter has the exact defect

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_s^H}\xi'-\xi
   &=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_{P_s}(\xi',H')}H,\\
 E_{P_s^H}(tH')-tH
   &=\frac{t\operatorname{Var}_{P_s}(H')}H.
 \end{aligned}                                \tag{6}
\]

These formulas require no differentiability, no regularity of a cap,
and no finite support for the (X)-law. All quantities are bounded
because the roofs are compact and their heights have a positive floor.

The physical lift is a martingale **if and only if**

\[
 H'=H\quad\Pi\text{-almost everywhere}.         \tag{7}
\]

Indeed, if the physical lift is a martingale then the second line of
(6), for almost every (t\ne0), forces zero conditional height variance.
Conversely (7) makes the height bias constant on each row, and (1)
then gives the full physical martingale property. Equivalently,

\[
 \int H^2\,d(\eta-\nu)
   =\int\operatorname{Var}_{P_s}(H')\,d\nu(s)=0. \tag{8}
\]

Thus the **neutrality** of the quadratic height test would give an
original-volume martingale. The actual convex-order hypothesis gives
only that its left side is nonnegative.

## 3. Exact projective correction, and why it adds no independent test

Define on the actual columns

\[
 \mathcal P(z,X,y)=
 \left(\frac z{H_z},\frac X{H_z},\frac y{H_z},\frac1{H_z}\right).
\]

The lift (3) is always a martingale in these projective coordinates:

\[
 E_{P_s^H}\mathcal P(w')=\mathcal P(w).         \tag{9}
\]

For example (E_{P_s^H}(\xi'/H')=\xi/H) and
(E_{P_s^H}(1/H')=1/H); the normalized vertical coordinate is the
same (t) on both sides. It follows that every convex test \(\varphi\)
on these coordinates satisfies

\[
 \int\varphi(\mathcal P(w))\,d\mu_W(w)
 \le\int\varphi(\mathcal P(w))\,d\mu(w).        \tag{10}
\]

This is an exact original-volume statement, but it is not an
additional consequence beyond the roof convex order. For fixed (t),
the roof function

\[
 (\xi,H)\longmapsto
 2H\,\varphi\!\left(\xi/H,t,1/H\right)
\]

is convex by the perspective construction, since its numerator vector
\((\xi,tH,1)\) is affine. Integrating this test in (t) gives (10)
directly from the original roof order. Moreover (z/H_z) need not be
integer. Neither lattice completeness nor a mixed center theorem may
be transferred through this map without an additional argument.

The first physical moment defect is also exact:

\[
 \int\xi\,d(\mu-\mu_W)
 =2\int\operatorname{Cov}_{P_s}(\xi',H')\,d\nu(s). \tag{11}
\]

The vertical first moments vanish by the common uniform (t)-law.

## 4. Why the linear roof flux returns the critical-budget identity

Let an actual ambient cap have continuous normal \((v,b)\ne0\).
Let \(A_z^+,A_z^-\) be its allocated captured roof areas and let
\(\lambda_H\) be its allocated continuous coarea section measure.
The latter includes the exact complement allocation on an inside
support and the exact equal allocation on an outside support. Applying
Gauss–Green to the vector field (y e_y) gives

\[
 \mu(H)=\sum_zH_z(A_z^++A_z^-)-b\int y\,d\lambda_H. \tag{12}
\]

This is the prism specialization of the archived polynomial flux
identity, not a new general divergence theorem. It remains valid with
supporting-facet allocations; replacing them by closed-cap indicators
would be incorrect.

Suppose a selected group has a common section (y)-mean (m_i) and
\(\omega_H T_H=\kappa_i\rho_H\), with
\(\sum_H\rho_H(v_H,b_H)=0\). Then its section correction in (12)
vanishes after weighting:

\[
 \sum_H\omega_H b_H\int y\,d\lambda_H
 =\kappa_i m_i\sum_H\rho_H b_H=0.               \tag{13}
\]

If all selected caps have mass (Q\) and the weights total one, (12)
therefore identifies (Q\) with the weighted roof expression. The
signed roof test (h_z=H_z), and its negative, are admissible because
every tight anchored height relation is an equality for this (h).
Their neutrality identifies the same roof expression with \(\beta M\).
Thus these two steps give precisely (Q=\beta M). They do not provide
an extra payment inequality.

Quadratic roof tests instead measure (8). Their sign need not be zero,
which is exactly the defect of the original-volume lift.

## 5. Actual compatible affine-roof calibration

Take (n=1,d=2), (P=\{0,1,2\}),

\[
 B_z=[-1/2,1/2],\qquad H_z=z+1.
\]

The canonical body is explicitly

\[
 C=\{(z,X,y):0\le z\le2, |X|\le1/2, |y|\le1+z\}.
\]

It is a convex body and the three stated fibers are all its integer
fibers. Their volumes are (2,4,6), so (M=12). Let the roof source
be three times the uniform measure on the middle upper roof. For each
(X), send its row equally to ((0,X,1),(1,X,2),(2,X,3)). This is an
actual same-normal, support-tight martingale: all three points lie on
the same exposed roof plane (y=1+z), and their mean is ((1,X,2)).

It can be written as (\nu=(W^+/\beta)\eta\) with
\(\beta=1/4\) and (W^+=(0,3/4,0)). Hence even the scalar bounds
\(0\le W^+\le1\) do not remove the defect. We do **not** claim this
particular (W^+) is a critical-cap stress; it is a counterexample to
deducing physical volume-martingale behavior from roof convex order,
support contact, and these bounds alone.

The volume lift has source density three on the middle fiber and zero
elsewhere. Its target is the actual original uniform mixed volume.
Its conditional target base probabilities are

\[
 (1/6,1/3,1/2),
\]

so its conditional target means are (E z'=4/3) and
(E H'=7/3). At source ((1,X,2t)), the physical drift is

\[
 (1/3,0,t/3).
\]

The quadratic roof gap is (14-12=2>0). The projective row means are
nevertheless exactly (E(z'/H')=1/2) and (E(1/H')=1/2).
The closed actual base halfspace (z\le1) has source mass 12 but
original target mass 6. Thus no monotone transfer of all cap masses
can be inferred from this lift either.

## 6. Exact surviving implication

The usable new equality implication is:

> A same-normal prism roof martingale whose quadratic height test is
> neutral lifts, by (3), to an actual original-volume martingale with
> source density (W^+/\beta\). Without neutrality, the full physical
> defect is (6), while the exact projective law is (9).

The signed roof stress provides the quadratic inequality, not its
neutrality. The actual critical-cap/source geometry would have to
supply that missing equality, or pay the explicit covariance defect.
The elementary flux identity (12) does not do so.
